experience.title: Creator & Lead Engineer
bullets: Researched autonomous agent fleets since mid-2025, starting with FSCPay (technical cofounder, LLM-powered payment processing), the first codebase run under my own orchestration. Built four generations of the controller: a Java daemon driving 50+ Claude Code agents, then a portable substrate with three-tier model routing, cross-machine memory in git, and rules moved out of prompts into config and gates.

After endpoint security kept wiping the machine mid-session, built the layer that tied it together: every rule, memory and checkpoint pushed continuously, heartbeat watchdogs, an IOC/secret-scan daemon, crash-only recovery from the remotes alone. That substrate became Aesop.

Architected Aesop (npm-published) with flat O(1)-depth dispatch: each worker in its own git worktree, bounded repair loops fed by real test failures, adversarial verification, single-writer state; 720+ PRs and 19 releases from ranked backlog to CI-verified merge with no human in the loop.

Evaluation and governance: pre-registered 5-tier benchmarks with hidden-oracle grading (+17pp one-shot solve from repro-in-context, ~4x cost cut at equal graded quality); kill switch, cost ceilings, fail-closed secret-scan and drift gates, event-sourced SQLite state, multi-model driver seam, MCP server and SSE dashboard.

experience.title: Software Engineer → Senior Software Engineer, People Analytics
bullets: Hired through AT&T's Technology Development Program onto People Analytics, a startup-style HR team building full-stack reporting products on the HR DataHub (Java/Spring Boot, Angular, Azure — millions of rows of SPI); operated as a lead developer from the start and promoted to Senior within the first year.
Designed HRMAN, a company-wide RBAC service grown from the team's user/role logic, serving tool-access control and real-time reporting-data authorization to teams across AT&T.

Initiated and led “Canned Reporting”: a config-driven reporting platform — report definitions live in the database over one generic frontend and backend; built the POC APIs and ran live demos of report creation, RBAC integration, and compound reports on a Java task-executor pool.
Shipped the PLE reporting tool for enterprise learning data — 1M+ reports delivered per year — and built stochastic workforce-modeling tools for HR planning.

Rearchitected backend cross-cutting concerns with Spring AOP — argument resolvers and exception handlers reduced authn/authz to a single annotation; rebuilt low-level result-set processing (HashMap-based) for a 40% memory reduction; introduced Redis caching to the team.
Grew the team from 5 to 12 developers as its first TDP — recruited through the program, mentored new hires, and wrote the onboarding guide that cut developer ramp-up from 3 days to 1.
Owned production releases and observability: Azure Application Insights monitoring and tracing saved ~20 developer-hours a month; served 8 months as Senior Scrum Master, lifting team velocity 27%.

experience.title: Technology & Operations Lead
bullets: Proposed and launched the company's leather sample-book product line, then scaled it into the full-time program I run today — engineering the swatch-book and leather-panel manufacturing processes and managing staff.

Engineered a Google Tag Manager “backend” for a backend-less Squarespace store: dynamic ads, organic listings, and a product-feed API built by treating page visits as tag-firing events through Google's own infrastructure; maintained to this day — online sales +10% YoY.
Own SEO end to end: grew organic Google traffic to rival direct traffic for the first time in company history; online sales rose 24% in my first three months back.

Built ECM-ai, an accounting tool that gamifies repairing bad order data so invoices import cleanly (a daily manual job became a monthly automated one), and TRTools, an internal RBAC-gated automation toolbox for all employees.

experience.title: UI/UX Developer / Co-Founder
bullets: Built and released the social media app “Glimpse” (Swift); won best in Illinois in the Verizon Innovative App Challenge and pitched the app to live audiences and investors — later rebranded and sold after my departure.
